title: Model admittance, pinflow, and profile broker for community weights
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Build a resilient end-to-end pipeline that admits community-provided model weights, performs deterministic conversion to Redwood runtime artifacts, runs validation and smoke suites, computes a canonical performance profile, and publishes a pinned model variant to the catalog. The pipeline should support: signed manifests, provenance metadata capture, resource-isolated conversion workers, automated pin recommendation (soft and hard modes), and a publish step that writes a performance profile and fingerprint to the model registry. The system must be usable for both hosted and private deployments and minimize manual operator interventions while providing clear audit trails.
motivation: We continue to see a growing volume of community weights. Manual handoffs are slow and error-prone. A unified automated path will reduce time-to-serve, surface regressions earlier, and enable predictable rollouts with performance SLAs.
design_decisions: Use signed manifests (PGP or signed JSON) to validate provenance before conversion
Run conversions in ephemeral, GPU-backed runners inside k8s jobs to isolate resource usage and improve reproducibility
Adopt deterministic artifact hashing after conversion to enable idempotent pin creation
Compute profile at multiple sequence-length buckets (64/256/1024) and publish latency/throughput/cost metrics
Separate "soft" pin recommendations from enforced pins: allow automated soft pins for canary flows and require manual approval for hard pins to tenant runtimes
tradeoffs: Aggressive automatic pinning speeds time-to-serve but risks releasing low-quality variants. Manual approval increases safety but adds latency. We chose a hybrid approach: publish profiles and a recommended pin automatically (soft pin), then gate hard pinning behind a short manual review or an automated quality gate for models with sufficiently high profile scores.
progress_updates: 2025-10-02: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and PM. Agreed on profile schema and essential telemetry fields.
2025-10-04: Prototype converter container completed (linux-x86 + CUDA 12). Initial smoke conversion for llama-2-7b compatible checkpoint succeeded.
2025-10-07: Integration test harness wired to Datadog sandbox; basic latency/throughput telemetry observed. Created initial profile publishing API spec.
2025-10-09: Security review scoping call; decided to require signed manifests for public community weights. Draft PR 1623 opened for conversion runner orchestration.
review_feedback: PM (Ravi Patel): Add end-to-end trace IDs across conversion + profiling steps so failures are easier to debug
Design (Lina Cho): Add a simple UX flag in Console for 'Recommended pin' vs 'Served pin' with tooltip explaining soft/hard semantics
Security (Priya Menon): Require artifact TTLs and ephemeral credentials for conversion runners; require KMS envelope encryption for intermediate blobs
open_questions: What minimum test coverage (which eval suite) qualifies a model for automated hard pinning?
How do we handle models with multiple variants (tensor parallel vs sharded checkpoints) — one pin per variant or grouped pins?
Edge-case: upstream license revocation after pin publish — what is rollback path and how to surface to customers?
acceptance_criteria: Given a signed community manifest, the pipeline converts weights to a Redwood runtime artifact reproducibly (same inputs -> same artifact hash)
Automated smoke suite completes within budgeted GPU minutes and produces pass/fail signals
Performance profile (latency p50/p95, throughput at 1,4,8 batch sizes, cost-per-token estimate) is computed and published to the catalog
A recommended soft-pin is published automatically and visible in Console with a human-readable rationale
Manual hard-pin workflow exists (review UI + audit log) and can be executed by authorized operators
Telemetry for conversion time, failure rates, profile variance, and pin adoption is available in Datadog dashboards
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Malformed community weights cause conversion worker failures. Mitigation: Run initial schema/manifest validation and resource-limited sandbox conversion before full run
Risk: Bad automated pins leading to customer regressions. Mitigation: Default to soft pins; require canary rollout and monitor QA metrics before hard pin
Risk: Sensitive data in upstream checkpoints. Mitigation: Enforce signed manifests with explicit 'contains-trained-data' flag and optional manual review for flagged models

estimated_cost_savings: Projected 15% reduction in manual triage time and 8% faster time-to-serve for community models after automation
safety_considerations: Ensure all automated profiles include a 'quality_score' and flag low-quality models to block default public serving; tie to existing safety review process for models tagged 'risky'
